specification.title: A unique violation is caught inside the transaction, which then ends normally
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Write the marker `tx`, and make sure the write was sent to PostgreSQL.
Checkpoint `after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(), read through the transaction's own connection.

Insert the value 'taken' into uniq through the framework's ordinary write API. It fails with unique_violation (23505). Catch the error and continue. After catching the error, the callback sends nothing else and returns.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. The transaction is aborted, so it cannot run queries; the runner confirms the aborted state server-side.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework sends COMMIT.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: When PostgreSQL has aborted the transaction before it ends, so that its COMMIT is answered with ROLLBACK, the API does not report a successful commit.

execution.description: Session.openSession and Transaction.begin on a DataSource that calls DriverManager.getConnection for every checkout and closes that connection on close. No pool. hibernate.dialect is not set; Hibernate selects the dialect from the connection. Flush mode is the Session default AUTO. hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto is none and jakarta.persistence.schema-generation.database.action is none. hibernate.jpa.compliance.transaction is false, the 7.4.13 default. The transaction coordinator is jdbc. Connection handling is DELAYED_ACQUISITION_AND_RELEASE_AFTER_TRANSACTION. TX-03 is not run in this mode: each Session checks out a new physical connection and session.close closes it, so a later unit cannot be handed that connection.

configuration.autocommit: Hibernate calls Connection.setAutoCommit(false) at begin when the provider has not disabled it, and setAutoCommit(true) in afterCompletion when it was on at begin

execution.form: Explicit Session.openSession, Session.beginTransaction, Session.persist, Session.flush, and Transaction.commit. Flush mode is the SessionFactory default. Schema generation is off. CTL-01.rollback and TX-03 call Transaction.rollback when the work throws and the transaction is still active. TX-01A catches the unique violation inside the transaction and then calls Transaction.commit. TX-01B calls Transaction.commit after the runner has terminated the backend. Identity is Session.doReturningWork on the transactional connection.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside the transaction, and caught by the application.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, before the transaction ends.
fault.preconditions: The row 'taken' already exists in uniq (fixture).
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction. PostgreSQL answers the later COMMIT with the command tag ROLLBACK, without an error, and commits nothing.
fault.expected_client: The driver receives the command tag ROLLBACK as the reply to COMMIT.

knowledge: The outcome reaches the client: PostgreSQL's reply to COMMIT carries the command tag ROLLBACK.

api_outcome.contract: Hibernate ORM 7.4.13.Final Transaction (org.hibernate.Transaction) is a resource-local transaction begun with Session.beginTransaction and ended with Transaction.commit or Transaction.rollback. The interface javadoc says there is at most one uncommitted transaction for a Session, and that after a rollback the persistence context must be discarded because Hibernate does not restore entity state. PostgreSQLDialect.causesRollback returns true, so JdbcCoordinatorImpl.afterFailedStatementExecution marks the JDBC transaction rollback-only when a statement throws SQLException. That call does not send ROLLBACK. JdbcResourceLocalTransactionCoordinatorImpl.commitRollbackOnly, when the transaction is MARKED_ROLLBACK, calls rollback and returns. It throws jakarta.persistence.RollbackException only when jpaCompliance.isJpaTransactionComplianceEnabled is true. hibernate.jpa.compliance.transaction defaults to hibernate.jpa.compliance, which defaults to false. This adapter sets both false and reads the flag back from the SessionFactory. AbstractLogicalConnectionImplementor.begin calls Connection.setAutoCommit(false) unless the provider already disabled autocommit. rollback calls Connection.rollback and then afterCompletion. If Connection.rollback throws, status becomes FAILED_ROLLBACK and afterCompletion is not called. afterCompletion calls Connection.setAutoCommit(true) only when autocommit was on at begin, then releases the connection when the handling mode is not ON_CLOSE. Session.inTransaction delegates to TransactionManagement.manageTransaction, which calls Transaction.rollback when the action throws and the transaction is still active. A returning Transaction.commit is reported as committed. A returning Transaction.rollback, followed by the application error leaving the boundary, is reported as rolled_back. An exception leaving the boundary is reported as failed. It is not a claim that PostgreSQL rolled back. TX-01A catches the statement error inside the work and then calls Transaction.commit. It does not call Transaction.rollback first.

violation.message: could not execute statement [ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_code_key" Detail: Key (code)=(taken) already exists.] [insert into uniq (code) values (?)]

evaluation.mechanism_detail: the session had closed when the API returned
evaluation.reason: TX-01A.1 violated: the API reported: committed

preconditions.description: the write of marker "tx" had reached PostgreSQL at `after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the duplicate insert failed with unique_violation (23505), as reported by the adapter
the top-level transaction was aborted before it ended: at `before-end` the session was "idle in transaction (aborted)" and pg_xact_status() already reported it aborted
PostgreSQL did not commit the transaction

invariants.statement: When PostgreSQL has aborted the transaction before it ends, so that its COMMIT is answered with ROLLBACK, the API does not report a successful commit.

invariants: TX-01A.1: When PostgreSQL has aborted the transaction before it ends, so that its COMMIT is answered with ROLLBACK, the API does not report a successful commit.
